title: Borrower-Requested Cancellation of Private Mortgage Insurance on Home Mortgage Loans
content:
The borrower on a Home Mortgage Loans note may request in writing that private mortgage insurance be cancelled once the loan-to-value on original value has come to the program's cancellation request figure or below it. Two further conditions attach to a request made on that ground.

**The loan must be current.**

**The payment history must be clean.** It must show no payment 30 or more days late over the months before the request that the program states for that test, and no payment 60 or more days late over the months before the request that the program states for its own. The history is read as the greatest number of days past due reached in each month of the window, taken from the loan's late charge and payment history in the bank's records.

## The conditions set out

| Condition | Basis on which it is judged |
|---|---|
| Loan-to-value on original value | At or below the program's cancellation request figure, taken on the original property value |
| Loan is current | The loan's standing in the bank's records |
| No payment 30 or more days late | Over the months before the request stated by the program for that test |
| No payment 60 or more days late | Over the months before the request stated by the program for that test |
| The request itself | Made in writing by the borrower |

## Basis questions

*Is a loan-to-value standing exactly at the program's cancellation request figure enough?* Yes. The condition is that the loan-to-value be at or below that figure, so the figure itself satisfies it.

*What decides the payment history?* The greatest number of days past due reached in each month of the window, drawn from the loan's own late charge and payment history rather than from an account the borrower gives of it.

*Do the two lateness tests run over the same window?* Not necessarily. Each runs over the months the program states for it, and the program carries the two figures separately.
